entries.title: Job 40:1
segments: ¶Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said,

entries.title: Job 40:2
segments: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct [him]? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

entries.title: Job 40:3
segments: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

entries.title: Job 40:4
segments: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.

entries.title: Job 40:5
segments: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

words.text: ; but I will proceed no further

entries.title: Job 40:6
segments: ¶Then answered the LORD unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

entries.title: Job 40:7
segments: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

entries.title: Job 40:8
segments: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?

words.text: me, that thou mayest be righteous

entries.title: Job 40:9
segments: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

entries.title: Job 40:10
segments: Deck thyself now [with] majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.

entries.title: Job 40:11
segments: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one [that is] proud, and abase him.

entries.title: Job 40:12
segments: Look on every one [that is] proud, [and] bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

entries.title: Job 40:13
segments: Hide them in the dust together; [and] bind their faces in secret.

entries.title: Job 40:14
segments: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.

words.text: unto thee that thine own right hand

entries.title: Job 40:15
segments: ¶Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox. {behemoth: probably an extinct animal of some kind}

words.text: . {behemoth: probably an extinct animal of some kind}

entries.title: Job 40:16
segments: Lo now, his strength [is] in his loins, and his force [is] in the navel of his belly.

entries.title: Job 40:17
segments: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together. {He...: or, He setteth up}

entries.title: Job 40:18
segments: His bones [are as] strong pieces of brass; his bones [are] like bars of iron.

entries.title: Job 40:19
segments: He [is] the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach [unto him].

entries.title: Job 40:20
segments: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.

entries.title: Job 40:21
segments: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.

entries.title: Job 40:22
segments: The shady trees cover him [with] their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.

entries.title: Job 40:23
segments: Behold, he drinketh up a river, [and] hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth. {he drinketh up: Heb. he oppresseth}

entries.title: Job 40:24
segments: He taketh it with his eyes: [his] nose pierceth through snares. {He...: or, Will any take him in his sight, or, bore his nose with a gin?}

words.text: . {He...: or, Will any take him in his sight, or, bore his nose with a gin?}
